source_quote: Chairperson: Lara Abou Orm
answer: The chairperson of the Computer, Math, and Sciences (CMS) Department is Lara Abou Orm. Full-time faculty: Professor Mahmoud Halablab; Associate Professor Houssam Salami; Assistant Professors Lara Abou Orm, Ali Rammal, Roaa Soloh; Instructor Roba Al-Hajj.

source_quote: The CMS Department offers two programs – Computer Science and Healthcare
answer: The CMS Department offers two programs, Computer Science and Healthcare Information Systems, each granting a Bachelor of Science degree.

source_quote: The vision of the Computer, Math, and Sciences (CMS) Department is to achieve
answer: The CMS Department's vision is to achieve academic excellence beyond accreditation standards in computing technologies and information systems.

source_quote: The mission of the Computer Science program is to provide students with a state-of-the-
answer: The CS program's mission is a state-of-the-art curriculum, industry relationships, professional responsibility and lifelong learning. Graduates are expected to solve computing problems for local/regional/global markets, show professional and ethical behavior, and progress in employment or graduate studies.

source_quote: Analyze a complex computing problem and apply principles of computing and other
answer: CS program outcomes: analyze complex computing problems; design, implement and evaluate computing solutions; communicate effectively; make informed legal and ethical judgments; work effectively in teams; and apply CS theory and software development fundamentals.

source_quote: The Bachelor of Science program in Computer Science is accredited by the Computing
answer: The BS in Computer Science is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission (CAC) of ABET under its General Criteria and Program Criteria for Computer Science.

source_quote: roles such as games developer, system analyst, software engineer, web designer,
answer: CS graduates work in industry, government, academia, TV stations and banking as games developers, system analysts, software engineers, web and mobile developers, database analysts/administrators, network engineers, data analysts, AI developers and IT consultants.

source_quote: To obtain a Bachelor of Science degree in CS, the student must complete 93 credit
answer: The BS in Computer Science requires 93 credit hours (University, College and Program requirements), planned over six semesters and two summer sessions.

source_quote: MATH 421 Numerical Analysis 3 MATH 311
answer: CS mathematics requirements: MATH 210 Discrete Mathematics, MATH 215 Calculus III, MATH 311 Linear Algebra, and MATH 421 Numerical Analysis (prerequisite MATH 311), 3 credits each.

source_quote: BMGT 300 Project Management 3 Junior Standing
answer: CS business requirements: BMKA 200 Introduction to Marketing (co-requisite ENGL 210) and BMGT 300 Project Management (Junior Standing).

source_quote: The CS mandatory core courses are listed in the table below.
answer: CS mandatory core: COSC 215, 231, 316, 333, 341, 351, 351L, 353, 360, 360L, 399 (Co-op), 421, 451, and 490 (Summative Learning Experience).

source_quote: As part of the Bachelor of Science in Computer Science program, students must take 9
answer: CS students take 9 credits of technical electives, chosen with the advisor, focusing on areas such as Internet and Computer Networks, Game Design and Development, AI and Data Mining, or Mobile/Web Design and Development.

source_quote: COSC 480 Machine Learning and Data 3 COSC 214; MATH 351 or
answer: CS elective courses: BITM 320, CCEE 426, CCEE 561 Computer Vision, CCEE 566 Natural Language Processing, COSC 434, 435, 436, 438, 461, 463, 480, 481, 482, 496, 497, 498, HCIS 341, HCIS 342, or any other approved CS elective.

source_quote: In addition, the students can take the following three labs instead of one elective.
answer: Instead of one elective, CS students can take three 1-credit networking labs: COSC 460L Networking Lab 2 (co-req COSC 360L), COSC 461L Networking Lab 3 (prereq COSC 460L), and COSC 462L Networking Lab 4 (co-req COSC 461L or CCEE 555L).

source_quote: Students must complete a 3-credit-hour course (COSC 490 Summative Learning
answer: CS students must complete COSC 490 Summative Learning Experience (3 credits), working preferably in groups on an industry/community problem or innovative idea, possibly extending earlier course projects.

source_quote: Each student must complete 8 weeks of practical training in a field related to their
answer: CS students complete 8 weeks of practical training, usually in the summer of the third year, matched by the Co-op office, followed by a faculty member, and submit a report and poster plus a presentation. ENGL 217 and senior standing are prerequisites; the program may add conditions.

source_quote: (COSC ABC), where:
answer: CS course codes are COSC ABC: A = year/level; B = area (1 Software, 2 CS Theory, 3 Mobile/Web Development, 4 Systems Analysis and Design, 5 Hardware, 6 Networking and Security); C = sequence in the area.

source_quote: Year 1, Semester 1 (15 Credits)
answer: CS Year 1 Semester 1 (15 credits): COSC 214, COSC 351, ENGL 210, MATH 215, and a Natural Sciences and Technology Elective.

source_quote: Year 1, Semester 2 (16 Credits)
answer: CS Year 1 Semester 2 (16 credits): ARAB 212, COSC 215, COSC 231, COSC 351L, a 1-credit Community & Sustainability course, ENGL 217, and MATH 210; then a summer session (3 credits) with a Humanities/Fine Arts Elective.

source_quote: Year 2, Semester 1 (16 Credits)
answer: CS Year 2 Semester 1 (16 credits): COSC 316, COSC 333, COSC 360, COSC 360L, MATH 351, and Social Science/Culture Elective I.

source_quote: Year 2, Semester 2 (15 Credits)
answer: CS Year 2 Semester 2 (15 credits): BMKA 200, COSC 341, MATH 311, and CS Major Electives I and II; followed by the summer session (1 credit) with COSC 399 Co-op Training Experience.

source_quote: Year 3, Semester 1 (15 Credits)
answer: CS Year 3 Semester 1 (15 credits): COSC 353, COSC 421, COSC 451, GRDS 440 Design and Social Impact, and Social Sciences/Culture Elective II.

source_quote: Year 3, Semester 2 (12 Credits)
answer: CS Year 3 Semester 2 (12 credits): BMGT 300, COSC 490 Summative Learning Experience, MATH 421, and CS Major Elective III.

source_quote: This course presents the fundamentals of structured and modular programming
answer: COSC 214 Introduction to Programming: structured and modular programming, primitive data types, expressions, control statements, functions, arrays, basic searching and sorting, and an introduction to pointers.

source_quote: COSC 214 Introduction to Programming 3(2,2)
answer: In the CS course descriptions, COSC 214 Introduction to Programming is 3 credits, 3(2,2): 2 lecture hours and 2 lab hours.

source_quote: Prerequisite: None. Equivalent to CCEE 214.
answer: COSC 214 Introduction to Programming has no prerequisite and is equivalent to CCEE 214.

source_quote: (OOP) languages and data structures. It covers pointers, classes, encapsulation,
answer: COSC 215 Advanced Programming and Data Structures, 3(2,2): object-oriented programming (pointers, classes, encapsulation, constructors/destructors, templates) and data structures such as stacks, queues, lists and trees.

source_quote: COSC 214. Equivalent to CCEE 216.
answer: COSC 215 requires COSC 214 and is equivalent to CCEE 216.

source_quote: implementing database systems. It covers database concepts, data modeling,
answer: COSC 231 Database Management Systems, 3(3,0): designing, using and implementing database systems, data modeling, relations, normalization and data manipulation languages.

source_quote: relations, normalization, and data manipulation languages. Prerequisite: COSC 214.
answer: The prerequisite for COSC 231 Database Management Systems is COSC 214.

source_quote: Equivalent to CCEE 315.
answer: COSC 231 Database Management Systems is equivalent to CCEE 315.

answer: COSC 316 Design and Analysis of Algorithms, 3(3,0): algorithm design and programming techniques, object-oriented properties, data structures, data abstraction and an introduction to complexity.

source_quote: abstraction, as well as an introduction to complexity considerations. Prerequisite:

answer: COSC 333 Web Programming, 3(3,0): front-end web development with HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript/jQuery and responsive design.

answer: COSC 333 Web Programming requires COSC 214 and is equivalent to CCEE 411.

answer: COSC 341 Software Engineering, 3(3,0): software process models, project management, requirements, SDLC stages, UML diagrams and CASE tools.

source_quote: 214. Equivalent to CCEE 310.
answer: COSC 341 Software Engineering requires COSC 214 and is equivalent to CCEE 310.

answer: COSC 351 Logic Design, 3(3,0): Boolean algebra, logic simplification, data representation, combinational circuits (decoders, encoders, multiplexers), sequential devices (flip-flops, registers, counters) and programmable logic devices.

source_quote: networks, including programmable logic devices. Prerequisite: None. Equivalent to
answer: COSC 351 Logic Design has no prerequisite and is equivalent to CCEE 221.

source_quote: This Lab covers design techniques and implementation of combinational and
answer: COSC 351L Logic Design Lab, 1(0,2): design and implementation of combinational and sequential logic circuits (gates, decoders, encoders, multiplexers, adders, flip-flops, registers, counters). Equivalent to CCEE 221L.

source_quote: This course exposes students to computer system organization and design;
answer: COSC 353 Computer Organization, 3(3,0): CPU datapath and control, instruction set design, memory hierarchy (caches, virtual memory), I/O subsystems, performance evaluation and pipelining.

source_quote: and pipelined processors. Prerequisite: COSC 351. Equivalent to CCEE 324.
answer: COSC 353 Computer Organization requires COSC 351 and is equivalent to CCEE 324.

answer: COSC 360 Networking, 3(3,0): fundamentals of computer networks, networking trade-offs, and designing and analyzing protocols.

answer: COSC 360L Networking Lab (1 credit) has COSC 360 as co-requisite.

source_quote: COSC 421 Theory of Computation 3 COSC 215 and
answer: COSC 421 Theory of Computation (3 credits) requires COSC 215 and MATH 210.

source_quote: COSC 451 Operating Systems 3 COSC 214
answer: COSC 451 Operating Systems (3 credits) requires COSC 214.

source_quote: COSC 490 Summative Learning Experience 3 ENGL 217
answer: COSC 490 Summative Learning Experience (3 credits) requires ENGL 217.

source_quote: COSC 399 Co-op Training Experience 1 ENGL 217;
answer: COSC 399 Co-op Training Experience (1 credit) requires ENGL 217 and senior standing.
